testCases: a pending exec transition is confirmed after readiness and remains recoverable after a daemon crash
a per-launch token distinguishes PID reuse even when start stamp and command collide
identity is revalidated before graceful and force signals
owned detached process groups are terminated once and removed only after confirmed exit
leaderless, unverifiable, timed-out, and failed cleanup records remain durable for retry
startup record failures and shutdown races cannot leave an untracked helper
tree-signal failures preserve retryable roots without regressing non-retrying callers
concurrent exec confirmation cannot recreate a removed record
patches.upstreamCondition: Submit independently while managed helper cleanup lacks per-launch identity, per-signal revalidation, explicit exec-transition confirmation, owned process-group cleanup, or durable retry state.
patches.dropCondition: Remove when the latest stable release verifies managed helpers with per-launch identity and start time, revalidates before each signal, cleans owned process groups once, and retains unverifiable or failed cleanup records.
